rory_pm: Quick decision thread 11 We need to prioritize three items for Private v1: signed airgap bundles (legal asked), a per-customer LB driver plugin model for on-prem IP preservation, and an automated compatibility matrix generator. Want explicit owners and whether they are MUST or NICE.

anika_eng: My take: MUST = signed bundles (supply chain), MUST = compatibility generator (preflight + UI badge), NICE = plugin model initially as a manual reconcile CLI. Plugin model is a bigger design and risky for v1.

omar_field: Field voice: large customers will demand the driver/plugin route because their netops won't allow cloud-style LB claims. If we punt plugin to NICE, expect longer sales cycles. They also want a short legal-signed install manifest they can hand to security teams.

syl_sre: From SRE: signed bundles are non-negotiable. For plugin model we can ship a minimal shim API that lets customers hook in a binary that implements a tiny interface: claimIP(service, desiredIP) -> result. That keeps us from shipping heavy plugins but satisfies netops for now. We should test shim in CI with a fake provider.

rory_pm: Decision: mark signed-airgap + compatibility-generator as MUST for v1. Plugin shim as MUST-OPTIONAL: ship shim API + reference shim implementation (not a broad marketplace). Owners: anika = signed bundle + compatibility automation (EOW), syl = shim API + fake-provider CI tests (two weeks), omar = field comms + security manifest template (EOD Tue).

anika_eng: Implementation notes: signed bundle = bundle.tar + bundle.sig using our release signing key; installer verifies signature and checks checksums. Compatibility generator will run preflight and produce a JSON card and a one-line badge status. I'll add an offline `--compat-report` mode that writes a tarball for airgapped handoff.

omar_field: Legal asked for a short install-attestation file that shows signature, bundle checksum, and installer-reported preflight hash. I'll coordinate with legal for phrasing. Legal-bot any guidance?

legal-bot: NOTE: legal reviewed and provided a short attestation template. They require the installer to record the bundle.sig fingerprint in the install log and provide a human-readable attestation.txt for the customer. See RW-LEGAL-55.

syl_sre: For upgrades: include a `--dry-run` that runs migration hooks, verifies LB claim path (or shim), and writes a reconciliation plan. Also we should produce a short audit log of IP rebind events. That helps customers and sales.

anika_eng: CI jobs: add a tiny k8s job that runs the shim fake-provider, exercises claim/reattach, and forces LB recreate to validate reconciliation. We'll gate the private packaging branch on that job.

rory_pm: Risk callouts: some customers will insist on vendor-signed shims; we will only provide reference shims. Mitigation: document how customers can sign their own shim binary and how to register the fingerprint in the installer. Also note that baked-in cloud APIs for IP claim won't work for metal LBs.

omar_field: Field ask: add an "onprem checklist" PDF that lists firewall rules, BGP hints, and the install-attestation snippet. I'll draft and attach to the roadmap doc.

syl_sre: Rollback/MTTR expectation: aim for <30m for common failures when using our shim; if customer builds custom shim complexity may exceed that SLA. We'll call that out in the compatibility card.

rory_pm: Action items: anika prototype signed-bundle + compat generator (due Fri); syl spec shim API + fake-provider CI (due in 2 weeks); omar draft attestation + onprem checklist (due Tue). I'll update the roadmap and tag epic "field-gates: signed-airgap, compat, shim-reference".

legal-bot: CREATED TASK RW-PRIV-3001: "attestation template + guidance" assigned to legal.

anika_eng: One more: include a small example config snippet for customer-managed networking in docs. I'll push it to the roadmap PR. Example: `network:
  mode: customer-managed
  ipClaim: shim://local-driver`

rory_pm: Great. If no objections, we'll lock this prioritization and inform sales/solutions. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
